title: MindForge Scholar — Bilingual ML Paper Review
description: A precision-built Korean/English paper-review template anchored by a single gradient mesh wave and mandatory purple-to-cyan section tags. Where every other seminar deck reaches for decoration, this one stays silent and lets the paper speak.
philosophy: This template exists for the Friday afternoon paper club — the kind where a graduate student walks through a transformer architecture to twelve colleagues who already read the abstract. It values typographic restraint and bilingual equity: Pretendard Korean and Latin letterforms are peers, never one subordinate to the other. It refuses illustration, iconography, and decorative noise on principle — only wave, gradient tag, and type survive the edit. The audience is there for the ideas; the slides should have the discipline to get out of the way.
goodFor: 15-slide ML or NLP paper review talks in university lab settings
Bilingual Korean/English seminar decks for mixed academic audiences
Dense methodology and equation slides that need visual calm
Conference-style reading group sessions requiring clean citeable structure
avoidFor: Investor pitch decks or commercial product launches needing strong brand personality
Workshops requiring illustrated explainers or playful iconography
Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews where data visualization dominates
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like the cover page of a carefully typeset preprint — deliberate silence punctuated by a single slow-rolling gradient wave that implies depth without demanding attention. Compositional weight leans left-center while the wave introduces asymmetric gravitational pull from below, giving the layout tension without decoration. The bilingual title pairing must read as two equals sharing one breath, neither language acting as a subordinate caption for the other. Resist any impulse to add texture, secondary shapes, or ornamental layering — the wave and the gradient tag chip are the complete visual budget for this slide.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with an 8–10% breathing outer margin on all sides. The gradient-mesh wave bleeds in from the lower-left quadrant, occupying roughly the bottom third of the canvas and receding behind the type layer — never competing with it. Title block places the English headline stacked directly above its Korean equivalent as a unified bilingual pair, anchored to columns 2–8 and positioned vertically center-left with a slight upward bias. A purple-to-cyan gradient tag chip sits two baseline steps above the paired title block, left-aligned to it; slide number appears at the far lower-right corner with no header band above.

examples.promptCore: The slide holds the restraint of a rigorously edited academic journal spread — no ornamentation survives beyond the gradient section tag and the barely-there wave at the lower margin. Compositional rhythm is vertical and deliberate: heading, rule, body, silence, page number — each element earns its place through function alone. The mood is late-seminar focus, the kind of attention a room gives when the methodology actually matters. Avoid any decorative layering, illustrative metaphor, or icon use; hierarchy must emerge entirely from scale contrast and the discipline of the structural rule line.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with an 8% outer margin on all sides; a narrow gradient pill tag (purple-to-cyan) anchors the top-left spanning cols 1–2, labeling the current paper section with a bilingual stacked pair treated as co-equal peers. Primary content occupies cols 2–11, opened by a compact heading row separated from the body zone by a single hairline rule. Body text may render as staggered bilingual runs inline, a tight bullet list, or an equation block — all share the same left spine at col 2 for visual unity. Page number sits flush bottom-right outside the content grid; the gradient mesh wave bleeds from the bottom edge at reduced opacity, never crossing the rule line.
